title: Phil Salt Steers Welsh Fire to Six-Wicket Win Over Southern Brave in Hundred Opener
excerpt: Captain Salt's unbeaten 47 anchors clinical chase of 136 at Southampton, while the women's match sees a dramatic late collapse as Southern Brave defend 126.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Phil Salt scored an unbeaten 47 off 37 balls, leading Welsh Fire to victory.
  • Southern Brave managed only 135 runs, with David Miller's late innings providing some resistance.
  • Welsh Fire's bowlers restricted Southern Brave effectively, with Nikhil Chaudhary taking 2/19.
  • In the women's match, Southern Brave won by eight runs after Welsh Fire's dramatic collapse.

Welsh Fire opened their 2026 Hundred campaign with a commanding six-wicket victory over Southern Brave at The Rose Bowl in Southampton on Wednesday, powered by a composed match-winning knock from captain Phil Salt.

Salt Anchors Clinical Chase

Winning the toss and electing to bowl on a surface that offered assistance to both pace and spin, Welsh Fire's bowlers delivered a disciplined performance that kept Southern Brave under pressure throughout their innings. The hosts stumbled early, losing Jamie Smith in just the second over, and never built the sustained partnerships needed to post a daunting total on a pitch described as offering sharp turn and swing.

Southern Brave's middle order labored to 92/4 at the drinks interval before South African veteran David Miller provided late impetus. Miller fell for a well-made contribution in the 20th set of five, however, and the hosts finished on 135/7 — competitive but below par on a ground that has historically rewarded positive stroke play.

Fire's Top Order Makes Light Work of Target

Welsh Fire's reply was built on intent from the outset. Matthew Short struck four boundaries in a brisk 20 off 15 balls during the Powerplay, helping his side to 37 in the opening 25 deliveries before falling to Daniel Worrall. Joe Root contributed a steady 15 before being run out through a sharp piece of fielding from Worrall and Smith.

"Salt dictated the tempo of the chase. His calm approach ensured the target was reached with six wickets in hand."

— CricketWorld match report

Salt, captaining the Fire for the first time in The Hundred, combined controlled aggression with intelligent shot selection. Alongside Ravindra — the New Zealand all-rounder who struck two boundaries in his rapid 24 off 16 — Salt guided Fire past the 100-mark with plenty of deliveries remaining. By the drinks break, Welsh Fire sat at 103/2, requiring just a handful of runs.

Women's Match Drama
›Georgia Voll scored 52 runs off 39 balls.
›Welsh Fire collapsed, losing 5 wickets for 6 runs.
›Sophie Molineux took 3 wickets for 14 runs.
›Southern Brave defended a total of 126 runs.

Though Ravindra and Jordan Cox fell in quick succession, with Indian youngster Nikhil Chaudhary picking up both scalps to finish with 2/19 for the Brave, the damage was already done. Salt remained unbeaten on 47, steering his side home with six wickets and two balls to spare.

Women's Match Delivers Late Drama

The evening encounter followed a thrilling afternoon in which Southern Brave Women defended 126 to beat Welsh Fire Women by eight runs. Georgia Voll's 39-ball 52 had Welsh Fire cruising at 109/3 before a remarkable collapse turned the match on its head.

Australian captain Sophie Molineux, fresh from leading her country to Women's World Cup glory, proved the difference with match-winning figures of 3/14. India's Jemimah Rodrigues contributed a crucial direct-hit run out of Freya Kemp that triggered the slide, while Lauren Bell claimed two wickets in three balls as Fire lost five wickets for just six runs in the space of 13 deliveries.

Diaspora Stars in Focus

The double-header showcased significant South Asian talent across both matches. India's Jemimah Rodrigues and Nikhil Chaudhary both made notable impacts — Rodrigues with her fielding brilliance in the women's match and Chaudhary as Southern Brave's most economical bowler in the men's contest. New Zealand's Rachin Ravindra, who has strong ties to India through his Bangalore-born father, was instrumental in the men's chase.

What's Next

Welsh Fire travel to Lord's to face London Spirit in their next fixture, while Southern Brave will look to bounce back when they host Trent Rockets. The Hundred's new ownership model — with Welsh Fire now backed by the Washington Freedom and Southern Brave under GMR Group — adds a fresh dynamic to English cricket's franchise competition as it enters its fifth season.
